lana: running quick nsys runs to repro a kernel-selection regression. small captures (500ms) pick weird kernels on the kv-prefetch path, looks like stride/affinity causes different kernels to fire. any tips on flags to get stable timelines?

mike: small captures often miss long-tail kernels. try longer duration + bracketed capture. also include osrt so scheduling shows up.

priya: for kv-prefetch specifically we saw sampling bias when the sample window overlapped warmup. two approaches: (1) bracket the hot window with --capture-range=bracket (warmup/active/teardown) or (2) disable sampling and use full tracing for that short section.

lana: thanks. bracket sounds right. still fuzzy on concrete CLI. sash, can you paste the exact nsys command you used for the prefetch trace?

sash: sure — this is what I used on the last run:

```
nsys profile --output=kv-prefetch-2259 \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=bracket --capture-range-end=stop \
  --sample=cpu --sample-freq=1000 \
  --duration=5s --force-overwrite --verbose -- python run_profile.py --workload kv_prefetch
```

sash: notes: --sample=cpu with freq=1000 gave consistent kernel timeline for both small and long kernels. duration 5s covers warmup+batches. change freq lower if file size blows up.

mike: small add: sometimes cpu sampling still misses fast microkernels. for those, use --sample=none and rely on cuda trace (or use perfetto GPU counters). but that increases file size. also try --sample=nvtx to bias samples around NVTX ranges.

priya: and set NVTX spans around the exact kv cache ops, e.g. nvtxRangePush("kv-prefetch") before and pop after. bracketed capture + NVTX gives you filtered view in timeline.

lana: helpful, thanks. one followup — kernel selection seems to flip between cublasLt matmul kernels when affinity differs. any way to coerce consistent kernel selection during capture?

mike: tune the GPU context/warmup to push the allocator into the same code path: 1) pin CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and set the same SM clocks (if possible), 2) run a short deterministic warmup batch before bracket start, 3) avoid concurrent processes. That usually stabilizes algorithmic kernel choice.

sash: also capture with `--osrt` + OSRT sampling enabled; OSRT will show CPU-side scheduling that often correlates with stride-driven prefetch ordering. helps explain kernel order even if CUDA trace alone looks random.

deploy-bot: build/2259 finished: artifacts at http://ci/internal/builds/2259 — contains run_profile.py used in captures.

lana: great. I'll re-run with sash's command, add an explicit warmup, and annotate NVTX around the kv prefetch. will post capture if it still looks inconsistent. :thumbsup:
